source_title: Might & Magic VI: The Mandate of Heaven
continuity_scope: The original English Windows PC release of Might & Magic VI: The Mandate of Heaven (1998), as witnessed by its credited 3DO/New World Computing user manual and getting-started card. This is the numbered sixth game only: earlier numbered games, Heroes, other Might & Magic spinoffs, later games, remasters/digital storefront builds, patches, adaptations, and other continuities are outside this pass.
work_or_witnesses: Might & Magic VI User Manual, written by D. G. Chichester; © 1998 The 3DO Company; New World Computing division credit
Might & Magic VI: The Mandate of Heaven Getting Started card, © 1998 The 3DO Company; New World Computing division credit
Ubisoft: Might and Magic brand page (current franchise ownership/orientation only)
coverage_rule: All individually named, plot-active dramatic agents who receive a specific role, action, kinship, appointment, investigation, rescue, command, or historical-conflict statement in the manual's Klavis Verge framing and its printed Roland letters (printed pp. 5–15): Klavis Verge, Roland Ironfist, Catherine, Nicolai, Kilburn, Acton Spindler, Aaron Hampton, Fineous Hogworth, Ragnar, Tanir, Sulman, Wilbur Humphrey, Rocklin, and Archibald. Player-created party members, generic followers, generic councilmen, unlabelled Oracle, unnamed messenger/stranger/necromancer, named places, factions, classes, creatures, spells, artifacts, and systems are excluded as non-nodes or insufficiently individualised by this witness.
omissions: All player-created or quick-start party members: the getting-started card says a player can create/change a party member's portrait, name, class, statistics, and skills, so they are variable rather than stable canonical NPC nodes.

Unnamed or collective figures, including the Oracle, Temple of Baa, council, gods, devils/demons, adventurers, Rangers, soldiers, NPC followers, the unnamed messenger, stranger, and prior castle owner.
Classes, skills, spell realms, races/species, monsters, artifacts, towns, Enroth, sci-fantasy interface metaphors, quests, all mechanics, and historical events as character nodes.

Might and Magic I–V, VII and later numbered games; Heroes and all other spinoff/reboot/continuity material; localized text; post-1998 patches, digital builds, mods, walkthroughs, fan wikis, Wikipedia, and database claims.
uncertainties: The original manual is accessed through non-rightsholder preservation hosts. It visibly bears 1998 3DO/New World Computing copyright/trademark notices, but host authorization, scan completeness, OCR fidelity, and current rights status are not independently established; each claim remains limited to clear manual text and page locators.
The current Ubisoft brand page confirms a broad franchise spanning many games, but it does not provide claim-level evidence for this 1998 game's characters and is not used for character assertions.

The manual's framing/letters are not a complete in-game NPC directory. This is a complete pass only for the stated manual-profile rule, not a claim that these are every named character encountered in a playthrough.

The letters contain pre-game history and possible outcomes; no ending, hidden identity, game-state result, or later-continuity fact is inferred. 'Queen Catherine' and 'King Roland' are used as the manual's names/titles without adding an unstated family name for Catherine.

The getting-started card describes both custom creation and a pregenerated-party option; neither supplies a fixed, named player-character cast. No player-avatar relationship edge or party outcome is asserted.
evidence_basis: Direct original-game documentation: a 1998 3DO/New World Computing copyrighted manual and getting-started card, consulted via preservation-host scans, plus Ubisoft's current high-level brand page for franchise breadth. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, secondary walkthrough, or community database is canonical evidence.
